# Affine width normalization and a same-base upper bound for hinge stress

This note replaces the Euclidean continuous-normal normalization in
`candidate de8d1a3251731edd`. It proves an
attained affine-covariant potential, its exact contact equations, a
shape-independent simplex-product calibration, and a conditional upper
bound retaining every cap-budget multiplier. It does not prove a global
OC budget or exclude abnormal Fritz--John multipliers.

Retain that note's finite positive `d`-dimensional fibers, `d>=1`, finite
cap count `N`, full-fiber closed coverage, cap budget `tau M`, and mixed
measure `mu`. Let `D subset R^d` be any fixed centrally symmetric convex
body with zero in its interior. For a nonvertical ambient margin

`L_i(z,x)=a_i dot z+u_i dot x-b_i`, `u_i!=0`,

define the scale-invariant objective

`Psi_D=sum_i [integral_S(L_i)_+dmu]/h_D(u_i)`.                  (1)

Multiplying one defining affine function by any positive scalar leaves
both the cap and its contribution to (1) unchanged. One may therefore
choose representatives satisfying `h_D(u_i)=1`.

## 1. Two different difference bodies and their exact covariance

Two useful choices must be distinguished:

`D_int=conv union_(z in P)(K_z-K_z)`,

and, when the fibers come from one convex body `C`,

`D_all={x-y:(z,x),(z,y) in C for some real z}`
`     ={v:(0,v) in C-C}`.                                    (2)

The second equality proves that `D_all` is compact, convex, and centrally
symmetric. Both are full-dimensional because a positive fiber contains
a continuous ball. One has `D_int subset D_all`; equality is NOT assumed.
In particular a difference formed by two means with the same REAL base
coordinate belongs to `D_all`, but need not belong to `D_int`.

Under a lattice-preserving fiber shear

`z'=Uz+k`, `x'=Ax+Bz+b`,

where `U` is unimodular integral, `k` integral, and `A` invertible, both
difference bodies transform to `A D`. The translations and fiber shear
cancel inside every same-base difference. If `u'=A^(-T)u`, the transformed
margin has coefficients

`a'=U^(-T)(a-B^T u')`,
`b_i'=b_i+u' dot b+a' dot k`,

and gives EXACTLY the same value at the corresponding points. Moreover

`h_(AD)(u')=h_D(u)`.

Every fiber volume, cap mass, and hinge integral is multiplied by
`|det A|`, independently of the fiber. Consequently `Psi_D/M` and all
normalized cap budgets are invariant under these transformations.
Every closed ambient halfspace is carried to a closed ambient halfspace,
and the integer lattice is preserved; no arbitrary affine mixing of the
integer coordinates into noninteger coordinates is used.

## 2. Attainment and positivity survive width normalization

If the cap-count/budget/full-cover class is nonempty, (1) attains a
strictly positive minimum. Indeed choose `r B_d subset D subset R B_d`.
The representatives `h_D(u_i)=1` satisfy

`1/R<=|u_i|<=1/r`.

Their directions therefore lie in a compact set bounded away from zero.
The threshold lower bounds, finite/infinite trace subsequence, and exact
kernel saturation proof from Section 1 of the continuous-normal note
apply verbatim, with these uniform bounds in place of `|u|=1`.
All limiting fiber cap boundaries have zero `d`-volume; closed coverage,
cap budgets, and hinge integrals pass exactly to the realized limit.

For an explicit positive lower bound, if `r_z B_d` is a translated
inball of `K_z`, a cap containing its center has hinge contribution at
least

`|u_i| kappa_(d-1) r_z^(d+1)/(d+1)`.

In the chosen representatives its denominator is one and `|u_i|>=1/R`.
Thus the attained potential is at least

`kappa_(d-1)/[(d+1)R] * sum_z r_z^(d+1)>0`.                    (3)

## 3. The support-point form of the joint equations

Use representatives with `h_D(u_i)=1` at a minimum, but allow arbitrary
nearby nonzero continuous normals and keep the quotient objective (1).
There is no unit-sphere constraint in this local formulation. The
objective's generalized gradient for cap `i` has the form

`(P_i, m_i-Psi_i R_i, -c_i)`,                                 (4)

where `c_i,P_i,m_i` are its actual cap mass and first moments, `Psi_i`
is its contribution to (1), and

`R_i in argmax_(v in D) u_i dot v`, `u_i dot R_i=1`.             (5)

Formula (4) follows by differentiating its smooth hinge numerator and
the reciprocal support-function denominator. The support-function
subgradient is the exposed face in (5); convex combinations remain in
that face. At a zero hinge contribution the multiplying term vanishes.

The cap-budget gradient has consistent actual coarea moments
`(P_i^s,m_i^s,-S_i)`, now with the factor `1/|u_i|`:

`S_i=sum_z (1/|u_i|) integral_(T_iz) theta_iz dH_(d-1)`,
`P_i^s=sum_z (z/|u_i|) integral_(T_iz) theta_iz dH_(d-1)`,
`m_i^s=sum_z (1/|u_i|) integral_(T_iz) x theta_iz dH_(d-1)`.

The densities are the same consistent supporting-facet traces as in
the earlier note; they cannot be chosen independently in the different
moment entries.

Apply its finite gradient-separation proof to the quotient objective,
cap budgets, and the full-fiber minimax certificates, allowing their
simplex weights `lambda_z` to vary. There exist nonnegative
`alpha_0,r_i,eta_z`, not all zero, and genuine contacts `x_z in K_z`
whenever `eta_z>0`, such that

`W_i:=alpha_0 c_i+r_i S_i=sum_z eta_z lambda_zi`,                (6)

`alpha_0 P_i+r_i P_i^s=sum_z eta_z lambda_zi z`,                 (7)

`alpha_0 m_i+r_i m_i^s
 =sum_z eta_z lambda_zi x_z+alpha_0 Psi_i R_i`.                 (8)

As before, `r_i>0` requires a saturated cap budget, `eta_z>0` requires
zero coverage margin, `lambda_zi>0` at such a contact requires
`L_i(z,x_z)=0`, and all other cap margins there are nonpositive.
The support force `-sum_i lambda_zi u_i` belongs to `N_Kz(x_z)`.
These assertions follow from the same joint certificate-weight equations,
not by assuming that every exposed point is a cap contact.

No sphere multiplier is present. Its role is replaced by the actual
support point `R_i` of `D`. The coefficient of the displacement is
exactly `alpha_0 Psi_i`. A possibly zero `alpha_0` is still retained;
changing the normalization has not proved a general constraint
qualification.

When `D=D_int`, an exposed point in (5) is a convex combination of
differences `p-q` in fibers whose `u_i` width attains the maximum width
over all integer fibers. In each summand `p` and `q` lie on the two
opposite supporting faces of the SAME fiber. It is not necessarily
one difference in one integer fiber. When `D=D_all`, (2) does represent
each `R_i` as a difference in one real fiber. Neither assertion turns
the support point `R_i` into a proposed mixed-integer center.

## 4. A genuine same-base upper bound when D=D_all

Suppose now that `S subset C` comes from a convex body and take `D_all`
in (1). Every stress satisfying (6)--(8) obeys

`alpha_0 Psi_i<=W_i=alpha_0 c_i+r_i S_i`.                       (9)

Proof. If `W_i=0`, the left side is zero by (6)--(8) and the cap/section
nonnegativity; equivalently if `alpha_0>0` then `c_i=0` and `Psi_i=0`.
Assume `W_i>0`. The positive measure consisting of `alpha_0` times the
cap restriction of `mu`, plus `r_i` times its consistent section trace,
has mass `W_i`. Its centroid belongs to `C` by convexity. The atomic
contact measure `sum_z eta_z lambda_zi delta_(z,x_z)` has the same
mass and also has its centroid in `C`.

By (7), these two centroids have exactly the same real base coordinate.
By (8), their continuous-coordinate difference is

`(alpha_0 Psi_i/W_i) R_i`.

It therefore belongs to `D_all` by (2). Evaluating its support in the
direction `u_i` and using (5) gives

`alpha_0 Psi_i/W_i<=h_Dall(u_i)=1`,

which is (9). No replacement of a real base coordinate by an integer
one has occurred. QED.

In fact the upper bound needs only (6)--(7) and the cap-contact equalities,
not the full vector identity (8). The two same-base centroids have
`u_i`-coordinate difference `alpha_0 Psi_i/W_i` directly: each section
and each positively weighted contact lies on `L_i=0`, whereas the cap
measure integrates `L_i` to `Psi_i`. Applying the width bound of their
common real fiber gives the same inequality. Thus (9) is already a
consequence of mass/base-moment transport plus actual boundary contact.

If `alpha_0>0`, scale it to one to write

`Psi_i<=c_i+r_i S_i`,
`Psi_D<=sum_i c_i+sum_i r_i S_i=sum_z eta_z`.                   (10)

The cap-budget multipliers have NOT been bounded or removed. In
particular (10) is not the generally stronger assertion `Psi_i<=c_i`.
Only when the corresponding `r_i` vanishes does that latter inequality
follow from this argument. The same proof does not apply with `D_int`
in place of `D_all` without an additional inclusion for the real-fiber
mean difference.

## 5. Exact shape-independent simplex-product calibration

For `C=[0,1]^n x K`, with `K` ANY `d`-simplex of volume `v`, one has
`D_int=D_all=K-K`. At the sharp individual cap budget `gamma_d v` and
cap count `2^n(d+1)`, the exact-cover classification in
`candidate 0e807db2bba0c137` forces exactly the
facet-parallel centroid cap of every vertex type in every integer fiber.

For a barycentric coordinate `lambda_j`, its continuous gradient
satisfies `h_(K-K)(grad lambda_j)=1`, because its range on `K` is
`[0,1]`. Thus the normalized canonical margin is just

`lambda_j-1/(d+1)`.

Its hinge integral is `v(d/(d+1))^(d+1)/(d+1)`. Summing all cap types
and integer fibers gives the exact minimum

`Psi_D=M (d/(d+1))^(d+1)=M gamma_d*d/(d+1)`.                    (11)

This value is independent of the shape and altitudes of the simplex.

There is moreover an explicit NORMALIZED joint stress for every simplex,
regular or not. Use `alpha_0=1`, all `r_i=0`, and at each binary fiber
use the centroid contact `g`, equal weights `lambda_zi=1/(d+1)` on
its own canonical cap types, and

`eta_z=(d+1) gamma_d v`.

For vertex `j`, let `g_j` be the centroid of its opposite facet and set

`R_j=vertex_j-g_j`.

It lies in the exposed face of `K-K` in direction `grad lambda_j`,
and that direction evaluates to one on it. The cap centroid equals

`g+(vertex_j-g)/(d+1)`.

Since `vertex_j-g=d(vertex_j-g_j)/(d+1)` and
`Psi_i/c_i=d/(d+1)^2`, the cap-centroid displacement is exactly
`(Psi_i/c_i) R_j`. Equations (6)--(8) follow directly; the continuous
certificate normals balance because `sum_j grad lambda_j=0`.
All other fibers have zero cap mass, so their moment contributions are
zero. This proves that the earlier Euclidean-normal abnormality for
nonregular simplex products does not survive the affine-width
normalization. It does not exclude other abnormal minimizing covers.

## 6. D_all loses positive dimension-only calibration on other sharp bodies

The distinction between `D_int` and `D_all` cannot be removed for free.
Here is an exact example with `n=2,d=1`. For `L>=0` give the four binary
fibers the unit intervals

`K_00=K_10=K_01=[0,1]`, `K_11=[L,L+1]`,

and let `C_L` be the convex hull of these four segments in `R^2 x R`.
Each binary base vertex is exposed in the square, so its actual fiber
in this convex hull is exactly the displayed interval. The integer
projection is exactly the four binary points and `M=4`.

At a real base `(s,t) in [0,1]^2`, the coefficient of vertex `(1,1)` in
a convex combination with that base can be any number in
`[max(0,s+t-1), min(s,t)]`. Hence the actual real fiber is

`[L max(0,s+t-1), L min(s,t)+1]`.

Its maximum width is `W=1+L/2`, attained at `(s,t)=(1/2,1/2)`.
Therefore

`D_int=[-1,1]`, `D_all=[-W,W]`.                                (12)

These bodies are OC-sharp for every `L`. The midpoint of each integer
interval has depth at least `(1/2)/4=1/8`, because any closed ambient
cap through it contains at least half of its own interval. Conversely,
at ANY point in an integer interval, choose the nearer endpoint side
of that interval and add a sufficiently large negative coefficient of
the affine binary-vertex distance `q_p(z)`. This isolates the chosen
fiber and keeps at most half of it. Thus the maximum depth is exactly
`1/8=2^(-2) gamma_1`, with all ambient caps included in the assertion.

At the sharp cap budget `1/2` and cap count eight, the same midpoint
cover argument as in the simplex-product calibration forces the two
midpoint half-interval caps on every integer fiber, with zero mass on
every other fiber. Their raw, `|u|=1` hinge total is `M/4`: each of the
eight caps contributes the integral `integral_0^(1/2) t dt=1/8`.
Normalization by `D_int` leaves this value unchanged, while normalization
by `D_all` divides every margin by `W`. Consequently the exact minima
in the two normalizations are

`Psi_Dint/M=1/4`, `Psi_Dall/M=1/[4(1+L/2)]`.                    (13)

In particular `Psi_Dall/M` tends to zero along bodies that all have the
exact OC depth constant. The same-base mean upper bound (9) is valid,
but it cannot be combined with a positive lower bound depending only
on `n,d` for this D_all-normalized hinge potential. D_int retains the
sharp calibration here, while the arbitrary same-real-base difference
used in Section 4 need not belong to D_int.
